newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thakral shines on earnings upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Thakral shines on earnings upgrade.

text.p: Thakral Corporation rose US$0.11 cents to hit a new year high of US$1.12 on Thursday as analysts upgraded the consumer electronic product distributor after good earnings for the year ended March 31, 1997.
At 0730 GMT, the stock was trading around US$1.09 with more than 1.90 million changing hands.
The group was listed on the Stock Exchange of Singapore in December 1995 at US$0.78.

Several analysts upgraded the company's stock further after it reported a net profit of Singapore $68.6 million, up 20 percent, which was on the upper side of the consensus. Turnover grew six percent to S$1.25 billion.
Analysts said prospects for the group, which has its main market in China, was bright.
According to the Edinburgh Financial Publishing's Estimate Directory, Thakral's net profit should be around S$77.8 million for 1998.
"The company is well-managed and seems to know what they are doing. It also has a strong China play. With that kind of critical mass, the potential is massive," said an analyst.
"Once there is a spark (in demand), there will be an explosion. It's all a matter of time," he added.
Thakral told reporters when announcing the results it intended to double its distribution network in China by the end of 1998, especially the rural areas where its presence is weak.
It also plans to expand manufacturing, currently around six percent of turnover, to double digits.
Some analysts said the stock could easily rise at least 10 percent in the coming weeks.
